newsitem.title: INDIA: Motorola, partners to invest in India.
newsitem.headline: Motorola, partners to invest in India.

text.p: Motorola Inc and its two partners in India's Spice Telecom, ModiCorp and Distacom Communications, said on Tuesday they plan to invest about 10 billion rupees ($280 million) over the next four years in India's Punjab state.

"Spice Telecom, a joint venture of ModiCorp of the Dr B.K. Modi Group, Distacom Communications of Hong Kong and Motorola of the United States today announced its plan to invest about 10 billion rupees over the next four years in Punjab," it said in a statement released in the Indian capital.
ModiCorp has a 51 percent stake in Spice Telecom. Distacom Communications owns 39 percent and Motorola holds 10 percent.
Spice Telecom has been licensed to operate mobile phone services in Punjab and Karnataka states.

Sean Dexter, head of Spice Telecom's operations in Punjab state, said the joint venture would be launching commercial service in the cities of Ludhiana, Jalandhar and Chandigarh in the next few months.
Service in Amritsar and Patiala would be launched soon after, he was quoted as saying.

The statement said Motorola had substantial presence in India as an equipment manufacturer and hardware supplier, but Spice Telecom was the only venture in which it had a direct stake as an equity partner.
